title: Belt conveyor speed control under payload change
algorithm: SIMC PI, payload-scheduled PI, static feed-forward, anti-windup

status.software: Executed from a clean kernel; local unit tests passed at build time; GitHub Actions has not been run on this repository

limitations: Illustrative parameters, not identified from a conveyor.
Single lumped mass: no belt elasticity or tension.
Items are captured instantly; real items slide for a short time.
Ideal load cell and ideal friction knowledge for feed-forward.
No stiction, no belt slip on the drive pulley.

checks.name: open-loop step matches scipy exact step (max error / final)
transfer-function poles equal state-matrix eigenvalues
steady speed at u=0.7 equals (F_max u - mu m g)/c, payload 0 kg
steady speed at u=0.7 equals (F_max u - mu m g)/c, payload 10 kg
steady speed at u=0.7 equals (F_max u - mu m g)/c, payload 30 kg
identified K within 1% of F_max/c
identified T + L within 3% of tau_m + tau_t (sum of time constants)
linear closed loop, payload 0 kg: error vs exact < 2% of step at Ts = 10 ms
linear closed loop, payload 0 kg: error halves when Ts halves (ratio 1.8 to 2.2)
linear closed loop, payload 30 kg: error vs exact < 2% of step at Ts = 10 ms
linear closed loop, payload 30 kg: error halves when Ts halves (ratio 1.8 to 2.2)
empty-tuned PI on 30 kg: simulated overshoot equals exact-model overshoot within 1 point
zero steady-state error for every controller and payload (startup)
30 kg startup rise time equals the force-limited formula within 5%
scheduled PI: small-step rise time varies less than 10% across payloads
fixed PI: same spread is more than 3x the scheduled spread
speed one sample after the drop equals the momentum prediction within 1.5% (all controllers)
scheduled PI recovers from the drop at least 2x faster than the empty-tuned PI
with back-calculation the speed saturates at the closed-form maximum within 1%
recovery time order after the reference drops: none > clamp > back-calculation
command peak-to-peak ripple is 0.7 to 1.3 times kp * (one encoder step)
speed ripple falls monotonically with encoder resolution
